text: [S1] So I showed up to the wrong wedding last year and didn't notice for fifteen minutes. [S2] How did you not realize? [S1] I thought I just didn't know anyone yet. I ate three appetizers. [S2] Did you sneak out? [S1] I tried. The father of the bride caught me at the door.

[S1] I accidentally ran a half marathon last spring. Grabbed the wrong bib at a 5K. [S2] And you just kept going? [S1] The gun went off and everyone started running. What was I supposed to do? [S2] Stop at the 5K finish line? [S1] That thought did not occur to me until kilometer eight.

[S1] I came face to face with a bear on a hiking trail last weekend. [S2] What did you do? [S1] Froze completely for about ten seconds while it stared at me. [S2] Did it come toward you? [S1] No, it just waddled off like I wasn't worth the effort. Honestly a little insulting.

[S1] I walked into a furniture store to return a lamp and the manager thought I was the regional inspector. [S2] And you played along? [S1] For about twenty minutes. I said things like the floor layout is very intuitive. [S2] How did it end? [S1] I had to sign a review form and that's when I came clean.

[S1] My cousin caught her hair on fire blowing out her birthday candles at a restaurant. [S2] Oh no, was she okay? [S1] Completely fine, just the tips. She looked up and said well that's one way to make an entrance. [S2] She kept her composure? [S1] Legendarily unflappable. We bring it up at every family dinner.

[S1] I went to Paris speaking zero French and immediately got a response I couldn't understand. [S2] What did you do? [S1] Just nodded. Ended up with six pastries I didn't order. [S2] Were they good at least? [S1] Incredible. Honestly the best possible outcome.

[S1] I left a novel in the office break room and accidentally started a book club. [S2] How? [S1] Someone left sticky note reactions in the margins and others started responding to them. [S2] That's genuinely sweet. [S1] Fourteen people showed up to the first meeting. We've been going eight months.

[S1] I signed up for pottery thinking it would be relaxing and got completely humbled. [S2] How bad was it? [S1] Every bowl collapsed. The woman next to me made a perfect vase on her first try. [S2] Had she done it before? [S1] Never touched clay in her life.

[S1] My neighbor has been learning violin for eight months and the walls are very thin. [S2] Is it bad? [S1] It was. But I've tracked his progress and I'm genuinely invested now. [S2] Do you talk to him? [S1] I told him I'd come to his first recital. I meant it.

[S1] Three of us drove to Montreal and none of us had booked a hotel. [S2] How does that happen? [S1] Everyone assumed someone else did. The city was sold out for a festival. [S2] Where did you end up? [S1] One room with one bed, one cot, and a large dog that chose me anyway.

[S1] What do you actually do as an air traffic controller? [S2] I manage aircraft in my sector, giving pilots clearances so nothing conflicts. [S1] How many planes at once? [S2] Ten to twenty five on a busy shift. You're always thinking a few minutes ahead. [S1] That sounds exhausting. [S2] You leave every shift feeling like you ran a mental marathon.

[S1] What does forensic accounting involve day to day? [S2] I trace money in fraud and embezzlement cases going to court. [S1] How do people usually get caught? [S2] Lifestyle inconsistency mostly. Someone earning sixty thousand a year buys a boat. [S1] Do you ever testify? [S2] Often. Translating financial evidence into something a jury can follow is half the job.

[S1] What's a typical day like as a marine biologist? [S2] Right now I'm up at six and diving by seven to survey coral reefs. [S1] How deep? [S2] Five to fifteen meters for this project. [S1] What happens after? [S2] Lab work mostly. There's a lot more desk time than people imagine.

[S1] What do city planners actually do? [S2] Shape how cities grow. Zoning, housing, transportation, long term development. [S1] Who do you work with? [S2] Everyone. Developers, politicians, community groups. A lot of it is facilitating disagreements. [S1] What's the most contested issue? [S2] Housing density. People support it in theory and object the moment it's near their street.

[S1] What does your day look like as a clinical research coordinator? [S2] I run the operations of a clinical trial. Enrolling participants, collecting data, following the protocol exactly. [S1] How strict is that? [S2] Every deviation gets documented and reported. [S1] What's hardest emotionally? [S2] When participants don't respond to treatment. You know these people. It doesn't get easier.

[S1] What does a structural engineer actually do? [S2] Make sure things don't fall down. I calculate forces and verify the structure can resist them. [S1] New buildings or old ones? [S2] Both. A lot of my work is retrofitting older buildings to current seismic standards. [S1] Is it collaborative? [S2] Constantly. I'm always coordinating with architects and contractors.

[S1] Is epidemiology basically disease detective work? [S2] For outbreaks yes, but mostly it's finding patterns in how disease is distributed across populations. [S1] What are you working on now? [S2] Air quality and respiratory hospital admissions across neighborhoods. [S1] How do you know if an effect is real? [S2] You build a case across multiple studies. No single result proves anything.

[S1] Is being a sommelier mostly recommending wine? [S2] That's a small part. I also manage the wine list, train staff, and negotiate with suppliers. [S1] How much is knowledge versus instinct? [S2] Both. Reading what a guest actually enjoys is more intuitive than people think. [S1] Biggest mistake people make ordering? [S2] Anchoring to price. Expensive doesn't always mean the right match.

[S1] What do you manage in logistics? [S2] Getting products from factories to shelves on time and within budget. When something breaks I fix it. [S1] What breaks most often? [S2] Inventory balance. Too much costs money, too little means empty shelves. [S1] How global is the operation? [S2] Very. I'm on calls before seven most mornings across three continents.

[S1] Is voice acting mostly doing funny voices? [S2] Not really. Most of my work is commercials and audiobooks where the goal is to sound natural. [S1] How do you find work? [S2] I send out fifteen to twenty auditions a week and book one or two. That's just the industry. [S1] What's hardest technically? [S2] Audiobooks. Thirty hours of consistent character voices with emotional stamina the whole way through.
